CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation for breast reduction surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for a new breast reduction consultation. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports symptomatic macromastia with back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain since high school. She experiences pain in the lower back and upper back that builds up, particularly when working at her desk all day. She has been seeing a chiropractor for a few years for this pain. She reports bra strap indentations on her shoulders and sometimes experiences numbness and tingling in her hands. She reports sweaty breasts but denies rashes underneath. She experiences activity limitations with working out, jumping, and running due to breast size and associated pain. She reports always sweating under her breasts. She currently wears a 34E sports bra as regular bras in her size are expensive and uncomfortable. She has not had any children but may plan to have children in the future. She has lost approximately 10 pounds over the past few months and would like to lose about 20 more pounds. She denies nipple pain or discharge.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
She sometimes experiences numbness and tingling in her hands. She denies rashes underneath her breasts. She reports her breasts are always sweaty. She denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Family history of breast cancer (mother diagnosed at age 40). Otherwise reports being healthy for the most part.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol (migraine medication).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother had breast cancer at age 40. Family history significant for breast cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently studying psychology at school. Drinks wine on occasion. Denies tobacco and drug use. No children currently.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. There is no nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable. Measurements obtained. One breast is noted to be slightly lower than the other. Patient currently wears approximately a G cup.

RESULTS
Body surface area (BSA) of 2.65. Minimum required resection based on Schnur scale is 1,792 grams. Physical exam findings consistent with symptomatic macromastia with severe bilateral ptosis. There is potential for using a nipple graft given extremely large breasts and measurements.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Patient attempted nonsurgical treatments with minimal relief. Goal breast size is approximately B cup, though expected outcome is likely small C cup given blood supply constraints. Surgery anticipated to take approximately 3 hours with bilateral drains to remain in place for approximately 1 week. Overnight hospital admission planned for pain and nausea management. Patient counseled on risks including potential inability to breastfeed (approximately 30% of patients), altered or absent nipple sensation, bruising, and activity restrictions for 6 weeks (no heavy lifting, no driving for 2-3 weeks). Patient counseled that breasts may change with weight gain, pregnancy, and aging. Scarring will be red initially and take approximately 1 year to mature and flatten. Plan to obtain photos today. Insurance approval will be submitted once patient switches to new insurance plan in July. Will schedule surgery date once insurance approval is obtained. Follow-up appointment to be scheduled prior to surgery for final questions and detailed preoperative instructions. Patient expressed readiness to proceed once insurance is switched over and will notify office when new insurance information is available.
